prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on what kind of coverage you need. Do you need individual/family (ACA marketplace), Medicare (Part A/B/D/Medigap), small‑business/group coverage, or something else? Also tell me your ZIP code (or whether you’re on the Kansas or Missouri side of Kansas City) and whether you prefer in‑person or virtual help — then I’ll find highly rated local brokers/agents and give tailored recommendations.

In the meantime, here’s how to find a great broker and what to ask them:

How to find a good broker in Kansas City
- Use official/local resources:
  - Healthcare.gov “Find Local Help” for ACA enrollment assistance.
  - Medicare.gov (or your state’s SHIP: State Health Insurance Assistance Program) for unbiased Medicare counselors.
  - National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) “Find an Agent” directory.
  - Your state insurance department website (Kansas Insurance Department or Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance) to verify licensing.
- Check local reviews on Google, Yelp, and the Better Business Bureau.
- Prefer independent brokers who represent multiple carriers rather than captive agents who only sell one insurer.

What to look for (qualities of a good broker)
- Licensed in Kansas and/or Missouri (verify on state website).
- Experience with the plan type you need (ACA, Medicare, small group).
- Willingness to compare multiple carriers and show total cost estimates (premiums + deductibles + out‑of‑pocket).
- Transparent about fees and commissions (some brokers are paid by carriers; ask if they charge clients).
- Availability to help after enrollment (claims help, renewals, special enrollment).
- Good local reputation and clear communication.

Questions to ask a broker
- Are you independent or do you represent a single insurer?
- Which carriers/plans do you typically work with for my situation?
- How do you get paid — do I owe any fees?
- Can you provide written plan comparisons and total cost estimates?
- Do you assist with claims and provider network verification after enrollment?
- How many clients like me have you helped recently?
- Can you enroll me and handle any appeals or special enrollment issues?

Red flags
- Pressure to buy a plan right away without showing options.
- Refusal to show written quotes or plan details.
- Unwillingness to confirm licensing or provide references.
- Vague answers about fees/commissions.

If you tell me your ZIP code and what type of plan you need, I’ll look up 3–5 well reviewed local brokers or agencies (with contact info and specialties) and recommend the best match for your situation.
